name: Latent Voxel Auto-Encoder
text:
# Latent Voxel Auto-Encoder

## Overview
The Latent Voxel Auto-Encoder (LAE) is a hierarchical neural network that compresses 3D voxel grids into a structured latent space consisting of a global 1D vector, a coarse 3D tensor, and a fine 2D tensor [S1]. It solves the dimensionality bottleneck of training [diffusion models](#10443-diffusion-models-ddpms.md) on high-resolution 3D data by reducing the representation size while preserving semantic structure [S1]. Unlike standard auto-encoders that map directly to a single latent space, LAE separates global scene properties from local geometric details using 2D CNNs applied to concatenated vertical slices, enabling efficient generation in [Hierarchical Latent Diffusion Models](17598-hierarchical-latent-diffusion-models.md).

## How it works
**Inputs and Outputs:**
*   **Input:** A voxel grid $V$ of size $128 \times 128 \times 32$ with 32 channels, containing concatenated density ($V_{Density}$) and feature ($V_{Feat}$) data [S1].
*   **Outputs:** Three latent variables:
    *   Global latent $g$: 1D vector of dimension 128 [S1].
    *   Coarse latent $c$: 3D tensor of shape $4 \times 32 \times 32 \times 16$ (channels $\times$ height $\times$ width $\times$ depth) [S1].
    *   Fine latent $f$: 2D tensor with spatial dimensions $128 \times 128$ and 4 channels [S1].
*   **Reconstruction:** The decoder outputs $\hat{V}$, the reconstructed voxel grid [S1].

**Data Structures and Layout:**
The input $V$ is processed by treating the vertical axis (Z, size 32) as part of the channel dimension. The input tensor to the encoders has shape $(32 \times 32) \times 128 \times 128$ [S1]. The architecture uses building blocks from VQGAN [S1]:
*   **ResBlock:** Two convolution layers, each preceded by Group Normalization and SiLU activation [S1].
*   **AttnBlock:** Self-attention module [S1].
*   **MidBlock:** Sequence of $\{ \text{ResBlock}, \text{AttnBlock}, \text{ResBlock} \}$ [S1].
*   **CGN Block:** A block where Group Normalization is replaced by Conditional Group Normalization, conditioned on $g$ [S1].
*   **Unet Connection:** Blocks prefixed with "Unet-" concatenate features from corresponding downsampling blocks [S1].

**Numbered Steps:**

1.  **Preprocessing:** Concatenate $V_{Density}$ and $V_{Feat}$ along the channel dimension to form $V$ [S1].
2.  **Vertical Concatenation:** Concatenate the vertical axis (Z) of $V$ along the channel dimension to create a 2D-compatible input tensor of shape $(32 \times 32) \times 128 \times 128$ [S1].
3.  **Global Latent Encoding ($g$):**
    *   Input: Concatenated $V$ [S1].
    *   Apply Conv2D $3 \times 3$ to get 128 channels [S1].
    *   Apply 6 iterations of $\{ \text{ResBlock}, \text{ResBlock}, \text{Conv2D } 3 \times 3 \text{ stride } 2 \}$ to reduce spatial size to $2 \times 2$ [S1].
    *   Apply $\{ \text{ResBlock}, \text{ResBlock}, \text{AttnBlock}, \text{MidBlock} \}$ [S1].
    *   Apply Conv2D $2 \times 2$ to get 256 channels [S1].
    *   Apply [Reparameterization](#11557-reparameterization.md) Trick to output $g$ (128-dim vector) with a KL penalty [S1].
4.  **Coarse Latent Encoding ($c$):**
    *   Input: Concatenated $V$ [S1].
    *   Apply Conv2D $3 \times 3$ to get 256 channels [S1].
    *   Apply 2 iterations of $\{ \text{ResBlock}, \text{ResBlock}, \text{Conv2D } 3 \times 3 \text{ stride } 2 \}$ to get $256 \times 32 \times 32$ [S1].
    *   Apply MidBlock [S1].
    *   Apply Conv2D $3 \times 3$ to get 32 channels [S1].
    *   Apply Unet-MidBlock [S1].
    *   Apply 2 iterations of $\{ \text{Unet-ResBlock-CGN}, \text{Unet-ResBlock-CGN}, \text{ResBlock-CGN}, \text{Upsample2x} \}$ to get $256 \times 128 \times 128$ [S1].
    *   Apply Conv2D $3 \times 3$ to get 4 channels [S1].
    *   Apply [Vector Quantization](#907-vector-quantization.md) (codebook size 1024) to output $c$ [S1].
5.  **Fine Latent Encoding ($f$):**
    *   Input: Concatenated $V$ [S1].
    *   Apply Conv2D $3 \times 3$ to get 512 channels [S1].
    *   Apply 2 iterations of $\{ \text{ResBlock}, \text{ResBlock}, \text{Conv2D } 3 \times 3 \text{ stride } 2 \}$ to get $512 \times 32 \times 32$ [S1].
    *   Apply $\{ \text{ResBlock}, \text{ResBlock}, \text{AttnBlock}, \text{MidBlock} \}$ [S1].
    *   Apply Conv2D $3 \times 3$ to get 32 channels [S1].
    *   Split the Z-axis back into 3D structure [S1].
    *   Apply Vector Quantization (codebook size 128) to output $f$ [S1].
6.  **Decoding:**
    *   Input: Concatenate $c$ along the vertical axis [S1].
    *   Apply Conv2D $3 \times 3$ to get 512 channels [S1].
    *   Apply $\{ \text{MidBlock-CGN}, \text{ResBlock-CGN}, \text{ResBlock-CGN}, \text{ResBlock-CGN} \}$ [S1].
    *   Apply 2 iterations of $\{ \text{ResBlock-CGN}, \text{ResBlock-CGN}, \text{ResBlock-CGN}, \text{Upsample2x} \}$ to get $512 \times 128 \times 128$ [S1].
    *   **Combine $f$:** Expand $f$'s channels to 128 using Conv2D $3 \times 3$, concatenate with the current tensor, then pass through three ResBlock-CGN layers to output $512 \times 128 \times 128$ [S1].
    *   Apply Conv2D $3 \times 3$ to get 32 channels [S1].
    *   Split Z-axis to reconstruct 3D shape [S1].
    *   Output $\hat{V}$ [S1].

**Formulas:**
The total loss $\mathcal{L}$ is defined as:
$$ \mathcal{L} = \mathcal{L}_{voxel} + 10 \cdot \mathcal{L}_{image} + \mathcal{L}_{KL} + \mathcal{L}_{VQ} $$

Where:
*   $\mathcal{L}_{voxel} = ||V - \hat{V}||$ [S1].
    *   $V$ is split into empty voxels and filled voxels. The loss is the mean of the reconstruction errors for these two groups summed together [S1].
    *   The reconstruction error for $V_{Density}$ is weighted 2.5$\times$ higher than for $V_{Feat}$ [S1].
*   $\mathcal{L}_{image} = ||i - \hat{i}||$, where $\hat{i} = r(\hat{V}, \kappa)$ is the rendered image from the reconstructed voxel [S1].
*   $\mathcal{L}_{KL}$ is the KL divergence penalty for $g$, multiplied by a coefficient of $2 \times 10^{-5}$ [S1].
*   $\mathcal{L}_{VQ}$ is the vector quantization loss for $c$ and $f$, multiplied by a coefficient of $1.0$ [S1].

**Parameters:**
*   **Optimizer:** Adam [S1].
*   **Learning Rate:** 0.0002 [S1].
*   **Codebook Size for $c$:** 1024 entries [S1].
*   **Codebook Size for $f$:** 128 entries [S1].

**Pitfalls and Edge Cases:**
*   The image reconstruction loss is used only to aid the learning of the LAE; the [scene auto-encoder](#17789-scene-auto-encoder.md) (renderer) used to generate $\hat{i}$ must be kept fixed during LAE training [S1].
*   2D CNNs are used instead of 3D CNNs for efficiency, requiring the specific vertical axis concatenation strategy [S1].

**Pseudocode:**

> **Unverified code.** The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors.

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

class ResBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, ch):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(ch, ch, 3, padding=1)
        self.norm1 = nn.GroupNorm(32, ch)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(ch, ch, 3, padding=1)
        self.norm2 = nn.GroupNorm(32, ch)
    def forward(self, x):
        h = F.silu(self.norm1(self.conv1(x)))
        h = self.norm2(self.conv2(h))
        return F.silu(h + x)

class AttnBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, ch):
        super().__init__()
        self.norm = nn.GroupNorm(32, ch)
        self.q = nn.Conv2d(ch, ch, 1)
        self.k = nn.Conv2d(ch, ch, 1)
        self.v = nn.Conv2d(ch, ch, 1)
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(ch, ch, 1)
    def forward(self, x):
        b, c, h, w = x.shape
        h = self.norm(x)
        q = self.q(h).reshape(b, c, -1).permute(0, 2, 1)
        k = self.k(h).reshape(b, c, -1)
        v = self.v(h).reshape(b, c, -1)
        attn = torch.bmm(q, k) * (c ** -0.5)
        attn = F.softmax(attn, dim=-1)
        h = torch.bmm(attn, v).permute(0, 2, 1).reshape(b, c, h, w)
        return x + self.proj(h)

class MidBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, ch):
        super().__init__()
        self.block1 = ResBlock(ch)
        self.attn = AttnBlock(ch)
        self.block2 = ResBlock(ch)
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.block1(x)
        x = self.attn(x)
        x = self.block2(x)
        return x

class ConditionalGroupNorm(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, ch, cond_dim):
        super().__init__()
        self.norm = nn.GroupNorm(32, ch)
        self.scale = nn.Linear(cond_dim, ch)
        self.shift = nn.Linear(cond_dim, ch)
    def forward(self, x, cond):
        h = self.norm(x)
        scale = self.scale(cond).unsqueeze(-1).unsqueeze(-1)
        shift = self.shift(cond).unsqueeze(-1).unsqueeze(-1)
        return h * (1 + scale) + shift

class VectorQuantizer(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_embeddings, embedding_dim):
        super().__init__()
        self.codebook = nn.Embedding(num_embeddings, embedding_dim)
    def forward(self, x):
        b, c, h, w = x.shape
        h_flat = x.permute(0, 2, 3, 1).reshape(-1, c)
        codebook_weights = self.codebook.weight
        dist = torch.sum(h_flat**2, dim=1, keepdim=True) + torch.sum(codebook_weights**2, dim=1) - 2 * torch.matmul(h_flat, codebook_weights.t())
        min_indices = torch.argmin(dist, dim=1)
        min_encodings = torch.zeros(h_flat.size(0), min_indices.size(0), device=x.device)
        min_encodings.scatter_(1, min_indices.unsqueeze(1), 1)
        q = torch.matmul(min_encodings, codebook_weights).reshape(b, h, w, c).permute(0, 3, 1, 2)
        q = x + (q - x).detach()
        return q, min_indices

class LAEEncoderGlobal(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv_in = nn.Conv2d(32*32, 128, 3, padding=1)
        self.downs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Sequential(ResBlock(128), ResBlock(128), nn.Conv2d(128, 128, 3, stride=2, padding=1)) for _ in range(6)])
        self.mid = MidBlock(128)
        self.conv_out = nn.Conv2d(128, 256, 2)
        self.mu = nn.Linear(256, 128)
        self.logvar = nn.Linear(256, 128)
    def forward(self, x):
        h = F.silu(self.conv_in(x))
        for down in self.downs: h = down(h)
        h = self.mid(h)
        h = F.silu(self.conv_out(h)).squeeze(-1).squeeze(-1)
        mu, logvar = self.mu(h), self.logvar(h)
        std = torch.exp(0.5 * logvar)
        g = mu + std * torch.randn_like(std)
        return g, mu, logvar

class LAEEncoderCoarse(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, codebook_size=1024):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv_in = nn.Conv2d(32*32, 256, 3, padding=1)
        self.downs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Sequential(ResBlock(256), ResBlock(256), nn.Conv2d(256, 256, 3, stride=2, padding=1)) for _ in range(2)])
        self.mid = MidBlock(256)
        self.conv_mid = nn.Conv2d(256, 32, 3, padding=1)
        self.skip_convs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(256, 256, 1) for _ in range(2)])
        self.ups = nn.ModuleList()
        for _ in range(2):
            self.ups.append(nn.Sequential(
                ConditionalGroupNorm(256, 128),
                ResBlock(256),
                ConditionalGroupNorm(256, 128),
                ResBlock(256),
                ConditionalGroupNorm(256, 128),
                nn.Upsample(scale_factor=2, mode='bilinear', align_corners=False)
            ))
        self.conv_out = nn.Conv2d(256, 4, 3, padding=1)
        self.quant = VectorQuantizer(codebook_size, 4)
    def forward(self, x, g):
        h = F.silu(self.conv_in(x))
        skips = []
        for i, down in enumerate(self.downs):
            h = down(h)
            skips.append(self.skip_convs[i](h))
        h = self.mid(h)
        h = F.silu(self.conv_mid(h))
        for i, up in enumerate(self.ups):
            h = up(h, g)
            h = torch.cat([h, skips[i]], dim=1)
            h = h[:, :256, :, :]
        h = self.conv_out(h)
        q, indices = self.quant(h)
        return q, indices

class LAEEncoderFine(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, codebook_size=128):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv_in = nn.Conv2d(32*32, 512, 3, padding=1)
        self.downs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Sequential(ResBlock(512), ResBlock(512), nn.Conv2d(512, 512, 3, stride=2, padding=1)) for _ in range(2)])
        self.mid = MidBlock(512)
        self.conv_out = nn.Conv2d(512, 32, 3, padding=1)
        self.quant = VectorQuantizer(codebook_size, 4)
    def forward(self, x):
        h = F.silu(self.conv_in(x))
        for down in self.downs: h = down(h)
        h = self.mid(h)
        h = F.silu(self.conv_out(h))
        # Split Z-axis: reshape from (B, 32, 32, 32) to (B, 4, 8, 32, 32)
        b, c, h_s, w_s = h.shape
        h = h.reshape(b, 4, 8, h_s, w_s)
        h = h.permute(0, 1, 4, 2, 3).reshape(b, 4, 8 * h_s, w_s) # Adjust to match table output 4x8x32x32
        q, indices = self.quant(h)
        return q, indices

class LAEDecoder(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv_in = nn.Conv2d(32, 512, 3, padding=1)
        self.mid = MidBlock(512)
        self.res1 = ConditionalGroupNorm(512, 128)
        self.res2 = ConditionalGroupNorm(512, 128)
        self.res3 = ConditionalGroupNorm(512, 128)
        self.ups = nn.ModuleList()
        for _ in range(2):
            self.ups.append(nn.Sequential(
                ConditionalGroupNorm(512, 128),
                ResBlock(512),
                ConditionalGroupNorm(512, 128),
                ResBlock(512),
                ConditionalGroupNorm(512, 128),
                ResBlock(512),
                nn.Upsample(scale_factor=2, mode='bilinear', align_corners=False)
            ))
        self.combine_f_conv = nn.Conv2d(4, 128, 3, padding=1)
        self.combine_f_res1 = ConditionalGroupNorm(1024, 128)
        self.combine_f_res2 = ConditionalGroupNorm(1024, 128)
        self.combine_f_res3 = ConditionalGroupNorm(1024, 128)
        self.conv_out = nn.Conv2d(1024, 32, 3, padding=1)
    def forward(self, c, f, g):
        # c shape: (B, 4, 8, 32, 32) -> Concat Z -> (B, 32, 32, 32)
        b, c_ch, z_ch, h_s, w_s = c.shape
        c = c.permute(0, 1, 3, 2, 4).reshape(b, c_ch * z_ch, h_s, w_s)
        h = F.silu(self.conv_in(c))
        h = self.mid(h)
        h = F.silu(self.res1(h, g))
        h = F.silu(self.res2(h, g))
        h = F.silu(self.res3(h, g))
        for up in self.ups: h = up(h, g)
        
        # Combine f
        f_exp = F.silu(self.combine_f_conv(f))
        h = torch.cat([h, f_exp], dim=1)
        h = F.silu(self.combine_f_res1(h, g))
        h = F.silu(self.combine_f_res2(h, g))
        h = F.silu(self.combine_f_res3(h, g))
        
        h = self.conv_out(h)
        # Split Z-axis to reconstruct 3D
        # Output shape should be 32x32x128x128
        return h

class LatentVoxelAutoEncoder(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.enc_g = LAEEncoderGlobal()
        self.enc_c = LAEEncoderCoarse()
        self.enc_f = LAEEncoderFine()
        self.dec = LAEDecoder()
    def forward(self, V):
        # V: (B, 32, 32, 128, 128)
        # Concat Z-axis: (B, 32*32, 128, 128)
        V_concat = V.permute(0, 2, 3, 1, 4).reshape(V.shape[0], -1, V.shape[3], V.shape[4])
        g, mu, logvar = self.enc_g(V_concat)
        c, _ = self.enc_c(V_concat, g)
        f, _ = self.enc_f(V_concat)
        V_hat = self.dec(c, f, g)
        return V_hat, g, c, f, mu, logvar
```

## Subtopics

### [Hierarchical Latent Diffusion Models](17598-hierarchical-latent-diffusion-models.md)
Generative models that fit a diffusion process to the compressed latents of LAE. They decompose the scene into global, coarse, and fine latent types, training separate conditional DDMs for each to generate complex 3D scenes.

## Operating characteristics
*   **Time and Memory Complexity:** The use of 2D CNNs instead of 3D CNNs reduces computational cost while maintaining similar performance [S1]. The hierarchical structure allows the diffusion model to operate on significantly smaller latent spaces (128-dim global, 4x32x32x16 coarse, 4x128x128 fine) compared to the raw voxel grid (128x128x32x32) [S1].
*   **Measured Performance:** The method enables the training of diffusion models on 3D scenes with resolution $128 \times 128 \times 32$ and 32 channels, which is larger than what standard diffusion models like Imagen handle for 2D images [S1].
*   **Strengths:** Efficient [compression](#4-compression.md) of 3D voxel data; separation of global and local features facilitates generation; 2D CNNs are more efficient than 3D CNNs [S1].
*   **Limitations:** Requires a fixed scene auto-encoder/renderer for the image reconstruction loss; relies on vector quantization which may introduce discretization artifacts [S1].
*   **When to use:** When generating or compressing high-resolution 3D voxel-based scenes where direct diffusion on raw voxels is infeasible [S1].
*   **When not to use:** When the scene auto-encoder/renderer is not available or cannot be kept fixed during training [S1].

## Background
The Latent Voxel Auto-Encoder was introduced in the context of NeuralField-LDM, a method for scene generation using [hierarchical latent diffusion models](#17598-hierarchical-latent-diffusion-models.md) [S1]. It addresses the challenge of high dimensionality in 3D [voxel representations](#19656-voxel-representation.md), which exceeds the capacity of standard diffusion models trained on 2D images [S1]. The architecture builds on building blocks from VQGAN and uses conditional group normalization to integrate global context into the decoding of local details [S1].

## Sources
